title: Finite-stalk set-sheaf constructibility from generic lissity on integral affine subschemes
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and $F$ a sheaf of sets on its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Suppose that for every integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] Noetherian affine scheme $S$ and every immersion $g:S\to X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], there is an open subset $W\subset S$ dense in $S$ such that $W\to S\to X$ pulls $F$ back to a finite locally constant sheaf, with finite geometric stalks. Then $F$ has a finite stratification into constructible locally closed subschemes on which its pullbacks are finite locally constant: $F$ is constructible in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. The dense-open hypothesis is stated using iterated set inverse images, as in [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image].

proof.text: Use well-founded induction on closed subsets $T$ of $X$, giving each its reduced induced closed subscheme. Prove that $F$ restricted to $T$ has a finite partition into locally closed subschemes whose restrictions are lisse. Closed induced subschemes and their opens are Noetherian, since they are locally of finite type over $X$ and quasi-compact; the empty $T$ has the empty partition.

If $T$ is reducible and nonempty, list its finitely many irreducible components $T_i$. Each is proper closed, so apply the induction hypothesis. For component $i$ restrict its strata to $T_i\setminus\bigcup_{j<i}T_j$. These are open restrictions of the old strata, so remain locally closed and lisse. Indeed an etale trivializing cover restricts to an etale cover, and the restriction comparison and inverse-image stalk bijection preserve constancy and finite stalks. The resulting finite partitions are disjoint and cover $T$.

If $T$ is irreducible and nonempty, its reduced induced scheme is integral. Choose a nonempty affine open $S$ of $T$. Apply the dense-open hypothesis to its composite immersion into $X$. The supplied dense open $W$ of $S$ is open and dense in $T$. Iterated and composite inverse images agree, so $F$ is lisse on $W$. The complement is proper closed in $T$ and closed in $X$; adjoin $W$ to its inductively supplied partition.

At $T=X$ with its reduced induced scheme structure, compose all stratum immersions into $X$. Their images partition $X$, and the inverse-image composition comparisons identify the restrictions with the lisse sheaves already constructed. All locally closed images are constructible because $X$ is Noetherian, giving precisely the Stratification witness required by the definition. There is no induction on Krull dimension.

lean.statement:
theorem isConstructibleEtaleSheafOfSets_of_generic_lisse
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X]
    (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (Type (u + 1)))
    (hF : ∀ (S : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral S] [IsNoetherian S] [IsAffine S]
      (g : S ⟶ X) [IsImmersion g],
      ∃ W : S.Opens, Dense (W : Set S) ∧
        IsLisseEtaleSheafOfSets
          ((etaleSetPullback W.ι).obj ((etaleSetPullback g).obj F))) :
    IsConstructibleEtaleSheafOfSets F
